تَجَعَلْهُ has a fatha on the jim it is تَجْعَلْهُ (taj'alhu).
'Free my neck' is form IV: تُعْتِقَ (tu'tiqa), not تَعْتِقَ.
اَجَزَ لَهٗ is one word split in two: اَجْزَلِهٖ (ajzalihi, 'most abundant'), genitive like اَتَمِّهٖ / اَعَمِّهٖ / اَوْسَعِهٖ before it.
اَهْنَاَهٗ should be genitive like the other elatives after عَلٰى: اَهْنَئِهٖ (ahna'ihi).
Governed by اَنْ, so subjunctive: يَنْقَضِيَ (yanqaḍiya).
فَزَعْتَ ('you fled') is a typo for فَزِعْتُ (fazi'tu, 'I fled to You').
مُحَمِّدٍ has a kasra on the mim it is مُحَمَّدٍ.
Final letter should be alif maqsura ى (as in هُدًى, هَوًى), not dotted ي.
شَيْءٌ is masculine, so the verb is يَكُوْنَ, not تَكُوْنَ.
Missing sukun on the jim: اَجْعَلَ.

A phrase seems missing: the pattern is 'refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, in Your pleasure from Your anger, in Your obedience from disobeying You' the standard wording is بِعَفْوِكَ مِنْ عُقُوْبَتِكَ. Please check the source book.
The usual formula is جَلَّ ثَنَاءُ وَجْهِكَ ('exalted is the praise of Your Face') ثَنَاؤُكَ وَ وَجْهُكَ looks like a corruption of it.

اَتَحَلَّلَهَا (subjunctive with no اَنْ) is ungrammatical. Most likely the masdar تَحَلُّلَهَا, parallel to اَدَاءَ ('I cannot repay it nor obtain release from it') otherwise indicative اَتَحَلَّلُهَا.
Istirja' (saying 'inna lillah...') is done at a calamity, الْمُصِيْبَةِ الْمَعْصِيَةِ ('sin') looks like a typo.
Missing hamza: خَطَأً (khaṭa'an), not خَطَا (khaṭā).
Governed by اَنْ, so subjunctive: اَشْتَرِيَ (ashtariya).
'Eating' goes with usury: اَكْلِ الرِّبَا (ar-ribā). الرِّيَاءِ (showing off) is listed separately later (وَ الشِّرْكِ وَ الرِّيَاءِ).
Ill omen is الطِّيَرَةِ (aṭ-ṭiyara) with kasra on the ṭa.
'Having few numbers in family and children' is not a sin most likely قِلَّةِ الْعَدْلِ ('lack of justice towards family and children'). Please check the source.
Missing tanween: بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ.
ت is a sun letter: التَّمَنِّيْ (at-tamannī), not الْتَمَنِّيْ.
Form VII masdar is wasl mid-sentence write a bare alif: وَ انْتِهَارِ.
Breaking an oath is الْحِنْثِ (al-ḥinth), kasra on the ha.
Oaths are الْاَيْمَانِ (al-aymān, plural of يَمِيْن) الْاِيْمَانِ means 'faith'.
Predicate of هُوَ, so nominative: مَعْصِيَةٌ.
وَ run into كُلِّ separate them like the rest of the text.
'In company' is مَلَإٍ (mala'in) مَلَاءٍ adds a long alif.
رَجَعَ يَرْجِعُ: اَرْجِعَ (arji'a), kasra on the jim.
Missing shadda: الصِّحَّةِ (aṣ-ṣiḥḥa).
بَهيٌّ lacks the kasra on ha: بَهِيٌّ (bahiyy).
برَحْمَتِكَ lacks the kasra on the ba: بِرَحْمَتِكَ.
مَشيئَتِكَ lacks the kasra on shin. Note line 25 writes the same word مَشِيَّتِكَ (the Mafatih spelling) the owner may want one spelling throughout.
كُلِّ must be nominative here (subject): وَكُلُّ مَشِيْئَتِكَ مَاضِيَةٌ, like every other 'wa kullu ...' line.
Mafatih reads بِاَحَبِّهَا اِلَيْكَ ('by the one most beloved to You') اِلَيْكَ seems dropped.
مِلْكِكَ should be مُلْكِكَ (mulk, dominion), as in the rest of the line and line 41.
بآيَاتِكَ lacks the kasra on the ba: بِآيَاتِكَ.
الشَاْنِ lacks the shadda of the sun letter: الشَّاْنِ (ash-sha'n).
كُلُّ is joined to بِكُلِّ and must be genitive: وَّ كُلِّ جَبَرُوْتٍ. (Mafatih reads بِكُلِّ شَاْنٍ وَحْدَهٗ وَ جَبَرُوْتٍ وَحْدَهَا this book's wording may be another version.)
عَامُّ lacks its tanween: عَامٌّ.
صَلَّي ends in dotted ya it should be alif maqsura ى: صَلَّى.
صَلَّي ends in dotted ya it should be alif maqsura ى: صَلَّى.
الملأ (al-mala', the host) has no long alif: الْمَلَاِ الْاَعْلٰى (al-mala-il a'la) الْمَلَاءِ reads 'al-malaa'i'.
Form IV imperative takes a fatha: اَعْطِ (a'ti), not اِعْطِ.
The standard phrase is قَنِّعْنِيْ بِمَا رَزَقْتَنِيْ (form II, 'make me content') اقْنِعْنِيْ is not a valid transitive form.
شَرِّ lacks its tanween: مِنْ كُلِّ شَرٍّ.
سُرُوْر (joy) has a damma on the sin, not a fatha.
مِن lacks the sukun on nun.
Marks swapped: sukun on nun and damma on waw should be بِنُوْرِ (bi-noori).
عَلَيَّ means 'upon me' the name is عَلِيٍّ (genitive, after وَلِيِّكَ).
Form VIII verb, hamzat al-wasl: انْتَجَبْتَهُمْ (alladhina-ntajabtahum), not اَنْتَجَبْتَهُمْ.
Shadda on the wrong letter: الْجَنَّةَ (al-janna).
اَعِيْنَ should be اُعِيْنَ (u'ina, form IV أعان: 'that I help against myself') the present of form IV takes damma on the alif
عَمَلَهَا is a typo for the verb عَمِلَهَا ('amilahā, 'whoever does it')
missing kasra on ت: عَبْرَتِيْ ('abratī, my tears)
the verb is صَمَتَ يَصْمُتُ, so the past is لَصَمَتُّ (la-samattu), not لَصَمُتُّ
after يَا اِلٰهِيْ the following title is also addressed, so غَايَةَ (ghāyata) is expected غَايَةُ only works if 'You are' is understood. Standard text not found to confirm
the word is نَقِمَة (naqima) or نِقْمَة (niqma) نَقْمَة with sukun is not the usual form (the Sahifa has نَقِمَة)
بَذُنُوْبِيْ should be بِذُنُوْبِيْ (bi-dhunūbī, for my sins): the preposition bi takes kasra
اَخِرِهِمَا is missing its long ā: آخِرِهِمَا (ākhirihimā, the last of them), as in آخِرَتِيْ later in the line
a vocative like this takes a plain damma, not tanween: يَا مَنَّانُ
the Quran (17:46) has عَلَىٰ with alif maqsura: عَلٰى
وَلَّوْا (wallaw, 'they turn') is one verb, not wa + لَّوْا (Quran 17:46)
same dotted ي in عَلٰٓي write it with alif maqsura عَلٰٓى as in the Quran
letters swapped: تَزْرُقُ for تَرْزُقُ (tarzuqu, You provide)
the verb is form I شَغَلَ يَشْغَلُ, so the imperative is اشْغَلْ (wash-ghal) اَشْغِلْ (form IV) is a rare usage. Check against the owner's source
missing sukun on ل: قَلْبَهٗ (qalbahū)
Sahifa 46 has يُخَيِّبُ (yukhayyibu, disappoint, form II) يُخِيْبُ is a typo
two errors: the ه of يَجْبَهُ is part of the root (j-b-h), so no silah sign ٗ and بِالرَّدِّ needs a shadda on ر (sun letter).
passive يُّشْكَرُ makes no sense here Sahifa 46 has the active يَشْكُرُ (yashkuru, 'who thanks for little')
Sahifa 46 reads يَشْكُرُ عَلَى الْقَلِيْلِ بِالْقَلِيْلِ may be a typist's echo of بِالْجَلِيْلِ that follows
Sahifa 46 reads يَدْنُوْ اِلٰى مَنْ دَنَا مِنْهُ ('who comes near to whoever comes near Him') يُدْنِيْ مَنْ ('brings near') still makes sense, so this may be a variant
missing sukun on ف: نَفْسِهٖ
يُغَيَّرُ is passive ('is changed') it must be active يُغَيِّرُ (yughayyiru, 'does not change the blessing')
Sahifa 46 vowels it بِالنَّقِمَةِ (naqima) نَقْمَة with sukun is not the usual form
Sahifa 46 has يُعَفِّيَهَا (yu'affiyahā, 'effaces it', form II), subjunctive after حَتّٰى like يُنْمِيَهَا before it
Sahifa 46 is vowelled الطَّلِبَاتِ (talibāt, plural of talibah) الطَّلَبَاتِ is also a valid plural of 'request', so the owner may keep it
Sahifa 46: وَتَفَسَّخَتْ دُوْنَ بُلُوْغِ نَعْتِكَ الصِّفَاتُ ('descriptions fall apart before reaching Your praise') تَفَتَّحَتْ ('opened') is a wrong word
a new sentence starts here, so كُلُّ needs damma, and Sahifa 46 has جَلِيْلٍ: كُلُّ جَلِيْلٍ عِنْدَكَ صَغِيْرٌ ('every majestic thing is small before You')
كُلُّ is the subject of حَقِيْرٌ, so damma: وَكُلُّ شَرِيْفٍ
missing tanween: قَرِيْبَةٌ (qarībatun) is the predicate
the verb is شَقِيَ يَشْقٰى, so يَشْقٰى (yashqā), not يَشْقِىْ
Sahifa 46 vowels it بِنَقِمَتِكَ (naqima)
Sahifa 46: وَحِلْمُكَ مُعْتَرِضٌ لِمَنْ نَاوَاكَ مُتَعَرِّضٌ looks copied from الْمُتَعَرِّضُوْنَ nearby
after مِنْ it must be genitive: مِنْ اَهْلِ الشَّقَاوَةِ
Sahifa 46 has خَذَلْتَهٗ لَهَا بِهَا may be a typist's echo of خَتَمْتَ لَهٗ بِهَا just before
Sahifa 46 has لَمْ يَهِنْ (from وَهَنَ, 'did not weaken') يَهُنْ (from هَانَ) means 'did not become lowly'
Sahifa 46 has the active لَمْ يَدْحَضْ (did not become void) the passive is grammatically possible, so low priority
the wonder form مَا اَفْعَلَهٗ has a hamzat al-qat': وَ مَا اَقْنَطَهٗ (wa mā aqnatahū)
marks on the wrong letter: the damma belongs on ج: تَجُوْرُ (tajūru)
missing sukun on ن: اِنْصَافًا
Sahifa 46 has الْاَعْذَارَ (al-a'dhār, the excuses) الْاِعْذَار (giving fair warning) is a possible reading, so the owner may keep it
Sahifa 46 has لِلْمُعَاجَلَةِ بِالْمُعَاجَلَةِ may be an echo of بِالْمُبَادَرَةِ that follows
form III masdar: مُدَارَاةً (mudārātan), with damma on م
missing shadda: اَقَلِّهٖ (aqallihī, the least of it)
Sahifa 46 has قَصَّرَ بِيَ السُّكُوْتُ ('silence has held me back'), with shadda
Sahifa 46 has فَهَّهَنِيَ (fahhahaniya, 'made me tongue-tied'): shadda on the first ه, and fatha on ي before the wasl
the ي carries a vowel here, so it must be dotted ي, not ى: قُصَارَايَ (qusārāya)
Sahifa 46 has لَا رَغْبَةً ... بَلْ عَجْزًا ('not from desire but from incapacity'), with tanween like عَجْزًا لَا رَغْبَةَ would mean 'there is no desire'
Sahifa 46 has اَؤُمُّكَ (a'ummuka, I head for You) اَرُوْمُكَ (I seek You) gives a similar meaning and may be a variant
the verb is خَتَمَ يَخْتِمُ: لَا تَخْتِمْ (lā takhtim)
after مِنْ it must be genitive: مِنْ عِنْدِكَ (min 'indika)
عَاجِزٍ is joined to ضَائِقٍ under غَيْرُ, so it is genitive: وَ لَا عَاجِزٍ (Sahifa 46)
this is the verb عَهِدَ ('which He enjoined upon us'), so عَهِدَهٗ ('ahidahū), not the noun عَهْدَهٗ
Standard (Iqbal / Mafatih, Ghadir ziyarah): اَوْصِيَاءِ اَنْبِيَائِكَ "the successors of Your prophets" اوصياء نبيك (plural successors of one prophet) is a slip.
Standard is passive حُمِّلَ (what he was charged with), parallel to اسْتُحْفِظَ / اسْتُوْدِعَ.
Final ya written dotted with a fatha before it should be alif maqsura صَلَّى (sallā).
وَالِيَ is a typo for the past verb وَالٰى (wālā, he befriended), parallel to عَادٰى.
Final dotted ya should be alif maqsura عَادٰى (ʿādā).
Mafatih/Iqbal read النَّاكِثِيْنَ عَنْ سَبِيْلِكَ (who broke away from Your path). فِيْ may be a variant.
A word is missing: standard is صَابِرًا مُحْتَسِبًا مُقْبِلًا غَيْرَ مُدْبِرٍ (advancing, never turning back).
Garbled: standard is شَهِيْدًا سَعِيْدًا وَلِيًّا تَقِيًّا (waliyyan) وَ علِيًّا also has no vowel on ع.
Standard reads رَضِيًّا (well-pleased) here, not وَصِيًّا.
Vocative with a following noun takes fatha: يَا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِيْنَ (yā rabba l-ʿālamīn).
تَصَرُّفُ is joined to the subject خَوَاطِرُ, so it takes damma (as in the standard text).
Marks misplaced: sukun on the alif and fatha on jim should be وَ اجْعَلْنِيْ.
Missing fatha on the final kaf.
Missing kasra on mim: مِمَّنْ.
The usual form is سَعِدَ (saʿida) سَعُدَ is rare.
Should be اَسْلَفْتُ (what I have done before), not اَسْلَفْتَ (what You did).
Wrong vowel on ya: يَحْبِسُ (yaḥbisu).
Prepositions swapped: standard is وَبِحِلْمِكَ مِنْ غَضَبِكَ (in Your forbearance from Your anger), parallel to بِعَفْوِكَ مِنْ عُقُوْبَتِكَ.
Standard: اَسْاَلُكَ بِكَ لَا بِشَيْءٍ هُوَ اَعْظَمُ مِنْكَ (by You, not by anything greater than You) the ب seems dropped.
Missing sukun on ع.
Imperative: فَسَلِّمْنَا (kasra on lam), like سَلِّمْنَا مِنْهُ right after سَلَّمْنَا would be 'we greeted'.
Imperative of قَبِلَ is wasl اقْبَلْ (and with a fatha on the alif it reads as a different word).
خِيْر is a typo for خَيْرٍ (khayr).
Missing shadda: تُحِبُّ.
ارْتِكَاب is a form VIII masdar (wasl) after بِ the alif is bare: بِارْتِكَابِ.
عَنِّيْ is repeated the second one should be وَ (فَلَا تَصْرِفْ عَنِّيْ وَجْهَكَ وَاجْعَلْنِيْ).
Form IV imperative takes hamzat al-qat': اَبْقِنِيْ (abqinī), like اَفْنِنِيْ after it.
Missing kasra on kaf: بِكِتَابِكَ.
رِيَاء is not a diptote (unlike خُيَلَاءَ), so it takes kasratain like the words around it: رِيَاءٍ.
The noun 'arrogance' is usually voweled بَذَخ (badhakh).
Should be مِنْ (of), not مَنْ. (Mafatih has وَاَنَا وَمَنْ لَمْ يَعْصِكَ سُكَّانُ اَرْضِكَ without مِنْ either way مَنْ is wrong.)
Imperative: سَلِّمْهُ (kasra on lam).
Extra وَ: الْمَبْرُوْرِ describes حُجَّاج (Mafatih: بَيْتِكَ الْحَرَامِ الْمَبْرُوْرِ حَجُّهُمْ).
Mid-sentence ال is wasl: no fatha on the alif, and the mim takes damma: حَجُّهُمُ الْمَشْكُوْرِ.
Same: wasl ال, so سَعْيُهُمُ الْ...
Same: wasl ال, so ذُنُوْبُهُمُ الْ...
Letters swapped: رَزَقَنَا (razaqanā, He provided for us).
تُطْفِىءُ is misspelled (dotless ya + loose hamza reads as a long ee) it is تُطْفِئُ (tutfi'u)
وَّ is run into غِنًى separate the words
عِزًا is missing the shadda: عِزًّا ('izzan)
two words run together: يَقِيْنًا يَسُدُّ
كُلِّ is the subject of يَتَيَسَّرُ, so كُلُّ (damma). (Some texts read تُيَسِّرُ لِيْ بِهٖ كُلَّ رَحْمَةٍ kasra is wrong either way)
شَيْءٍ is the subject of لَا يَكُوْنَ, so شَيْءٌ (shay'un)
الْعَمَلَ continues مِنْ طَاعَتِكَ وَ خَشْيَتِكَ, so genitive: الْعَمَلِ
same as الْعَمَلِ: genitive التَّرْكِ
مِنْكَ ('from You') makes no sense here it is قَدِيْمِ مَنِّكَ ('Your age-old favour')
subjunctive like the verbs around it (اَنْ ... تُنَجِّيَنِيْ وَ تَمُنَّ): تُوَسِّعَ
Mafatih and most texts read الْكَذِبِ (al-kadhib) الْكِذْب is a rare but attested form, so owner may keep it
the al- of الْحَجَّ is wasl mid-sentence
كُلِّ is the subject of the verb: كُلُّ شَيْءٍ (same in the next three lines)
subject of ذَلَّ: كُلُّ
subject of اسْتَسْلَمَ: كُلُّ
subject of خَضَعَ: كُلُّ
Allah is the subject: صَلَّى اللّٰهُ (sallal laahu)
الَّذِيْن lacks its fatha
عِنْدَ takes a fatha: عِنْدَكَ ('indaka)
indefinite like شَقِيٌّ and مَحْرُوْمٌ before it: مُقَتَّرٌ (muqattarun)
sukun on the mim instead of kasra: الرَّاحِمِيْنَ
ش is a sun letter: الشِّدَّةِ needs the shadda
يَنْفَذُ (with ذ, 'pierces') is a typo for يَنْفَدُ (with د, 'runs out'): نَعِيْمًا لَا يَنْفَدُ
idafa, so no tanween: جَنَّةِ الْخُلْدِ (jannatil khuld)
missing sukun on ض: فَضْلِكَ
the fixed phrase is لَا مَلْجَاَ وَ لَا مَنْجٰى مِنْكَ اِلَّا اِلَيْكَ (manjā, 'place of escape'), not مُنْجِيْ ('rescuer')
فَيْمَا is a typo for فِيْمَا (fīmā, 'in what has passed').
Lam needs kasra: تُصَلِّيَ (tuṣalliya), not the passive-looking تُصَلَّيَ.
اَكْفٰي is not a word here the standard phrase is مَا اَكُفُّ بِهٖ وَجْهِيْ ('what I may keep my face from begging with').
Mim is missing its fatha: اَمَلَاهُ (amalāh, 'O my hope')
After اَسْاَلُكَ the verb needs اَنْ and the subjunctive fatha: اَنْ لَّا تُشَوِّهَ, matching the following وَ اَنْ تَقْضِيَ and the standard text.
Needs tanween, like بِفَاحِشَةٍ before it: بِصَالِحٍ (bi-ṣāliḥin).
Conditional 'if': اِنْ وَعَدَنِيْ كَذَبَنِيْ (in wa'adanī), like the other اِنْ clauses around it.
After اِلَّا (= اِنْ لَا, 'if not') the verb is jussive: تَصْرِفْ, like تُفْلِتْنِيْ.
Jussive after اِلَّا: تَعْصِمْنِيْ (ta'ṣimnī).
Answer of the condition should be jussive: يَسْتَزِلَّنِيْ (yastazillanī). The damma form reads as indicative. (يَصُدُّنِيْ can stay: damma is allowed there.)
بِكَ is a typo for لَكَ: 'to You belongs all praise', parallel to وَ لَكَ الْمُلْكُ.
كُلّ follows the genitive الشَّاْنِ, so كُلِّهٖ (kullih).
After مِنَ الْخَيْرِ it must be genitive: كُلِّهٖ.
After مِنَ الشَّرِّ it must be genitive: كُلِّهٖ.
Sad has no fatha: صَلِّ.
The usual reading is فِيْ قَدَرِكَ (qadarika, 'Your decree'), as in other copies of this line قَدْر is possible but less likely.
The usual text has the subjunctive after حَتّٰى: لَا اُحِبَّ (uḥibba). The damma is grammatically possible.
Object of لَا تُوَلِّ, so accusative: غَيْرَكَ (ghayraka).
Ra is missing its kasra: مِنَ الْاَمْرِ.
Shadda missing: لَا يُرَدُّ (lā yuraddu).
Subject of the passive الْمُكَفَّرِ عَنْهُمْ, so nominative: سَيِّئَاتُهُمْ (sayyi'ātuhum), like حَجُّهُمُ and ذُنُوْبُهُمُ before it.
pause added before the new اَللّٰهُمَّ

questions: Dua 9: وَ كُلِّ رَسُوْلٍ اَرْسَلَهٗ اِلَيْهِ - 'every messenger He sent to Him' reads oddly the parallel phrases have اَنْزَلَهُ اللّٰهُ / اَظْهَرَهُ اللّٰهُ, so the source may have اَرْسَلَهُ اللّٰهُ. Could not find the dua online to confirm please check the printed book.

Dua 9: قَرِيْنِ سُوْءٍ مُكْدٍ and وَ مِنْ مُرْدٍ اِلَى النَّارِ could not be checked against a source (dua not found online) مُكْدٍ is plausible, مُرْدٍ before اِلَى النَّارِ is reported as a likely مَرَدٍّ (unsure).
Dua 9: مِّمَّا اسْتَعَاذَ بِهٖ رَسُوْلُكَ - earlier lines use اسْتَعَاذَ مِنْهُ ('sought refuge from') بِهٖ ('sought refuge in') may be a slip for مِنْهُ. Left as is.

Sentence 2: الْمُتَهَجِّدُوْنَ ... الْمُؤْثِرُوْنَ فِيْ ذِكْرِكَ, and اَعَنْتَهُمْ without a preceding الَّذِيْنَ. Some texts may read المجتهدون / الموقرون ذكرك / الذين أعنتهم. I left these as typed, since they read grammatically.

Sentence 11: وَ حَقَّ عَلَيْكَ is left as typed. It could also be the noun وَ حَقٌّ عَلَيْكَ check it against the book.
Dua 39 وَ لَا تُذِلَّنَا بَعْدَ اِذْ عَزَّزْتَنَا: many texts have اَعْزَزْتَنَا (form IV). عَزَّزْتَنَا (form II) is valid Arabic, so I left it unchanged. The owner should check the source.
Dua 39 بُلِيَ بِهَا is valid (the passive of بَلَا). Some texts may have ابْتُلِيَ. I left it unchanged.

Dua 15 is the Ghadir-day dua from Iqbal al-A'mal (Mafatih only points to it). Compared with an Iqbal text, the book drops several phrases. These may come from a shorter edition, so they are not listed as fixes: وَ مَنْ كُنْتُ وَلِيَّهٗ فَعَلِيٌّ وَلِيُّهٗ (sentence 3) وَ دَيَّانُ دِيْنِكَ after بَعْدَ نَبِيِّكَ (6) لَنَا in جَدَّدْتَ لَنَا عَهْدَكَ (6) وَ جَعَلْتَهٗ فِيْ اُمِّ الْكِتَابِ لَدَيْكَ عَلِيًّا حَكِيْمًا and الَّذِيْ هُمْ فِيْهِ مُخْتَلِفُوْنَ (9) اِلٰى يَوْمِ الدِّيْنِ after اِمَامًا (10) the second مُسَلِّمِيْنَ in مُسْلِمِيْنَ مُسَلِّمِيْنَ مُصَدِّقِيْنَ (14) وَ اجْعَلْنَا before تَحْتَ رَايَتِهٖ (17). The owner should decide whether to restore them.
Sentence 5: فَاشْهَدْ يَا اِلٰهِيْ ('so bear witness, my God') against Iqbal's فأشهد ('so I bear witness'). Both read well, so it was left as is.
Sentence 2: صَلَّي and sentence 15: صَلَّي are written with a dotted ي instead of ى. This was left as is.

Line 52: Mafatih reads بِمَا تُجِيْبُنِيْ بِهٖ حِيْنَ اَسْاَلُكَ فَاَجِبْنِيْ يَا اَللّٰهُ this book omits بِهٖ and فَاَجِبْنِيْ.
